title: These Bees Gave Up Flowers. They Eat Dead Animals and Still Make Honey

scenes.text: These bees don't collect pollen. They eat dead animals.
Only three species are known, all stingless bees from the tropics. Scientists call them vulture bees.
They slice off flesh with toothed jaws and carry it home in the leg baskets other bees fill with pollen.
In Costa Rica, researchers hung raw chicken from branches at sixteen bait stations. The bees came for it.
Their guts turned out to be full of acid-loving bacteria, like the ones found in real vultures and hyenas.
Back at the nest, the meat is sealed in chambers for two weeks. And in separate pots, they still make honey. It's reportedly sweet.

description:
Vulture bees are tropical stingless bees that feed on carrion instead of pollen; only three such species are known. They cut meat with toothed mandibles and carry it in the hind-leg baskets other bees use for pollen.
In a 2021 study in Costa Rica, researchers baited them with raw chicken at 16 stations and found their gut bacteria resemble those of vultures and hyenas. The meat is stored in sealed chambers for about two weeks, separate from the honey, which is reportedly still sweet and edible.
Would you taste honey made by meat-eating bees?
